findings.title: Malformed Evolution observations can release managed cleanup without proving absence
findings.rationale: EvolutionHttpClient.consultarInstancia at evolution.client.ts:79–84 treats every non-array successful response as an empty inventory and returns null; chamar at :145 also converts invalid JSON to {}. ChannelsService interprets that null as conclusive absence and records CLEANED at channels.service.ts:61, :174 and :484 without successful deletion. Thus a successful HTTP response with malformed or contradictory content can clear CLEANUP_PENDING for an existing managed instance, after which another INITIAL may create a replacement without resolving the old resource. The current staged-unlink repair depends on this shared observation contract, while its fake returns null only for actual inventory absence and does not expose the distinction. The adapter and the older INITIAL null-to-CLEANED behavior predate CP1 and remain byte-exact inherited source; this is not attributed as a CP1-introduced regression. No explicit disposition or waiver of malformed observation semantics was found. It nevertheless limits the current claim that cleanup uncertainty survives until reconciliation.
findings.suggested_action: Keep cleanup pending when observation is inconclusive. Distinguish validated absence from malformed or contradictory responses, or require positively confirmed exact-resource deletion before clearing the fence. Add a causal lifecycle case using the real adapter with synthetic HTTP responses, proving malformed observation preserves the cleanup record and blocks another create while a valid absence/deletion can complete recovery. Obtain explicit source admission before changing the immutable adapter dependency if that repair requires it.
